subject: Trish Schiapelli City Council Candidacy
overview: John Petrella interviewed City Council candidate Trish Schiapelli regarding her platform, which emphasizes financial accountability and opposition to current rezoning plans. Schiapelli called for a forensic audit of city finances and criticized the management of the recent tax override and infrastructure projects.

items.title: Introduction and Background
items.summary: Trish Schiapelli discussed her professional background as a commercial lender with an MBA and her residency in Medford since 2009.

items.title: Candidacy and Primary Concerns
items.summary: Schiapelli outlined her reasons for running, citing concerns over city mismanagement, rising taxes, and a perceived downward spiral in infrastructure quality.

items.title: Proposed Solutions for City Governance
items.summary: The candidate proposed firing the city's zoning consultants and planning officials while urging voters to replace current council members with independent candidates.

items.title: Financial Standards and Meeting Procedures
items.summary: Schiapelli advocated for a forensic audit, 21st-century financial reporting standards, and a return to weekly City Council meetings to increase transparency.

items.title: Zoning and Property Rights
items.summary: Discussion focused on protecting property owners' rights against radical rezoning and shifting toward a 'smart growth' model similar to neighboring towns.

items.title: Economic Growth and Negotiation
items.summary: Schiapelli recommended improving the city's business friendliness and using better negotiation tactics to retain commercial tax revenue from properties like the Budweiser campus.

items.title: Criticism of Divestment Debates
items.summary: The candidate criticized a recent four-hour City Council session regarding international divestment, labeling it a diversion from local mismanagement.

items.title: Audit Proposals and Advisory Boards
items.summary: Schiapelli proposed hiring a specialized forensic accounting firm and establishing industry-expert advisory boards to guide municipal financial and planning decisions.

items.title: Tax Override and Voter Information
items.summary: The candidate criticized the implementation of the seven and a half million dollar override, alleging the process was opaque and that tax calculators provided to the public were inaccurate.

items.title: Personal Preferences and Closing
items.summary: Schiapelli identified the public library as her favorite city asset and provided her campaign contact information.
